prior_outcomes_observed: All earlier source outcomes including foundation global/centre/consensus pooling; no confirmatory holdout claim
inputs: Fixed DINOv2 RGB/depth global descriptors from foundation_pooling_v1, unchanged 151 events and group splits
base_kernels: Separate RBF kernels for RGB and depth; each training pairwise median squared distance sets its bandwidth, times [0.5,1,2]
group_weights: 1 divided by the number of training episodes from that animal group, normalised to sum one; only for kernel alignment unless explicitly marked unbalanced
ordinal_target: Binary cumulative code z_ik=1(y_i>k), k=2,3,4,5; target kernel Z Z^T. No invented new ordinal loss or first kernel-alignment claim.
alignment: Weighted centring H=I-1 w^T, A_m=diag(sqrt(w)) H K_m H^T diag(sqrt(w)); unit Frobenius norms. Solve nonnegative two-variable quadratic min(v^T M v - 2 a^T v), M_mn=<A_m,A_n>, a_m=<A_m,A_y>, ridge=1e-8. Normalise v to sum one and combine the original PSD RBF kernels.
SVR: epsilon=.1, C=1/alpha, alpha in [.01,.1,1,10]; inner-validation MAE selects bandwidth and C, target labels used for alignment come only from training groups
shuffled_control: Fixed permutation of training labels only for alignment target, true training labels still used by SVR; all permutations saved
uncertainty: Animal-group paired bootstrap of out-of-fold event errors, conditional on fitted models; report effects versus equal kernel mixture and same-encoder concatenation
novelty_scope: Application-specific adaptation of established alignment learning to repeated-animal ordinal BCS data; effectiveness must exceed matched controls before being called a useful new method
